assertions: The husband is alive at the time of the question — he has not drowned, died at sea, or been lost with his ship
The husband is in good health and complete safety: his significator the Sun, in its hayz and free from all affliction, shows no sickness, captivity, shipwreck or mortal danger upon him
The husband is still abroad at sea / away on his voyage, not yet home
The husband will return home safely — his return is assured and he himself comes back unharmed
The wife will not live to see or enjoy his return home
The wife herself will die on or about 8 October following the question

Her death comes from her own chronic, relapsing illness — Saturn, lord of her 6th, retrograde, relapsing from one disease into another, brought to a fatal crisis by the approaching ill aspect of Mars and Saturn — not from any harm to her husband
summary: Her husband is alive, well and will return safely, but she herself will die on about 8 October following, before she can see him home again.
method: Lilly classical horary astrology, whole-house: Sun as the husband's significator, Saturn lord of the querent's 6th for her disease and fate from the same figure
reasoning: Sun as husband's significator in hayz and wholly free from affliction = a living, healthy, safe man with a safe return assured. Against this, the wife's own figure is fatal: Saturn lord of her 6th retrograde signifies chronic relapsing disease (with her smallpox disfigurement, weak eyes and grief already given), and Mars and Saturn moving to an ill aspect, timed by the Moon's position relative to Mars (about 2 degrees) and Saturn in about 2 degrees of Capricorn with the Moon then at about 20 degrees, perfects her fatal crisis on 8 October following — hence a safe husband, but a querent who dies before his return.
